patch.value: Parallel jobs must not replace the shared global npm

Deep and release workflows install the pinned npm globally after setup-node. On the shared local runners every container on a host shares the toolcache Node installation, so parallel jobs replace the same npm and fail with ENOTEMPTY or npm: command not found. GitHub issue unbraind/pm-ops#284.

Every workflow installs the pinned npm with --prefix into a job-local directory and prepends its bin to the job path, keeping the exact-version assertion; A workflow-contract test fails if any workflow replaces the global npm; A regression test runs two overlapping pinned installs into separate prefixes against one shared Node directory and proves both stay at the pin with the shared npm untouched

value.text:
Round AF follow-up on the fail-closed guard, from the pm-ado review threads PRRT_kwDOUMUq1864PGRG and PRRT_kwDOUMUq1864P73_ and the identical pm-lint threads PRRT_kwDOVHTnEc64QBn2, PRRT_kwDOVHTnEc64QBn6 and PRRT_kwDOVHTnEc64QBn7; this repository carries the same guard with the direct YAML dependency. All three findings were reproduced against the guard source first: a prefix bootstrap followed by '&& npm install -g npm@11.19.0', 'npm install -gpld npm@11.19.0' and step env NPM_CONFIG_GLOBAL=true were all accepted by the previous code.

1. Segment-scoped prefix exception: run scripts now split into command segments at unquoted ;, &, | and newlines. The scanner tracks quote state across lines and $( … ) substitutions (which nest a fresh quoting context even inside double quotes), skips comments and here-document bodies (the workflow-scoped test in this repository uses here-documents, which are now skipped as non-delimiting text), and any script that cannot be delimited (unbalanced quote or substitution) fails closed as 'undelimitable command line'. The job-local prefix exception only covers the segment carrying it; rejected fixtures add 'npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/npm-11.19.0" npm@11.19.0 && npm install -g npm@11.19.0' and 'npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/npm-local" npm@11.19.0; npm install -g npm@11.19.0'. Approved bootstrap fixtures stay accepted.
2. Combined short flags: any single-dash letter cluster containing g now marks global (rejected: 'npm install -gpld npm@11.19.0', 'npm install -dg npm@11.19.0'); 'npm install -D pnpm' and 'npm install -gpld pnpm' stay accepted.
3. Workflow, job and step env compose for each step run, the step scope taking precedence; npm reads npm_config_* keys case-insensitively. npm_config_global set to anything other than false/0/empty, npm_config_location=global, a ${{ … }} expression value, or an unreadable env scope or entry forces every npm install in that run global unless its own segment carries a job-local prefix. Fixtures cover step env flow mapping, job env flow and block styles, workflow env, expression values, location=global, step-override (job "true" + step "false" accepted) and accepted "false"/"0"/"" values.

Gates: guard suite 62 passed; the workflow-scoped job-local-npm test ('no workflow replaces the shared global npm installation') passed, its subprocess-based pinned-install integration test is unchanged and left to CI; typecheck, test build, lint, duplication and changelog:check passed. Every workflow in the repository still scans clean; the ../subprocess.ts wrapper in the job-local tests is untouched. Full-suite certification remains with CI.
